description: Stop each SLSQP run early via a callback once the sum of radii has not improved by more than 1e-6 for 10 consecutive iterations, so more random restarts fit in the time budget.

Abort the Variable Step Repair idea: a cooling step size in _repair would only trim small overlaps left after SLSQP, so it cannot move the mean sum of radii beyond the 0.0034 noise, and damped shrinking risks leaving overlaps that crash the harness.
Before the shrink loop in _repair, first move overlapping centres apart in place (clipped to the box) for up to 20 steps, so that fewer radii have to be shrunk.
Gradual radius scaling: run SLSQP in stages with a cap on every radius (0.1, 0.2, 0.35, 0.5, then 1.0), warm-starting each stage from the previous one, to avoid early local optima.

Replace the uniform random centre initialisation in _solve_once with a scrambled Sobol low-discrepancy sequence (seeded from the existing rng, so each restart still differs) mapped into the same [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW] box, for better initial coverage.

Replace the SLSQP overlap constraints in _solve_once with a penalty objective (sum of radii minus a growing weight times squared overlaps and boundary violations), optimised by L-BFGS-B over increasing penalty weights, with the existing repair step kept to guarantee validity.
Iterative shrink-and-grow: after each solve and repair, grow the repaired radii by 2% and re-solve from that packing for two extra rounds, keeping the best result within the time budget.
Restrict the _repair step to only the circles that are out of bounds or overlapping, but I am aborting because the current code already does this implicitly.
After each repair, re-run a short SLSQP pass (10 iterations, radius cap 1.0) warm-started from the repaired packing, then repair again, so the shrinkage is partly recovered.
Abort the Elastic Band repair idea: the repair step only trims tiny SLSQP tolerance violations, so spring-based centre relaxation would not change the packing in any measurable way.

Sequential Circle Addition: each restart builds the packing up from 1 circle, adding one random circle at a time and re-optimising all circles with SLSQP, with the full radius-cap schedule applied only at the final n.

Sequential Radius Growth: in each staged SLSQP pass, apply the radius cap only to the currently smallest circles (a growing fraction of n per stage, reaching all circles in the last stage), so large circles are not constrained early.

Greedy initial placement: each start places circles one by one at the best of 200 random candidate points (largest free radius), replacing the uniform random centre and radius initialisation before the staged SLSQP.

Boundary-aware initialization: draw the initial centre coordinates from a Beta(0.5, 0.5) distribution rescaled to the same range, so starts cluster near the edges and corners instead of spreading uniformly.

Add basin hopping: after the first restart, each iteration with probability 0.7 perturbs the best packing with Gaussian jitter (sd 0.02) on centres and radii and refines it with 50 SLSQP iterations, otherwise it runs a full staged restart.

Boundary-aware initialization (drawing initial centres from a distribution that favours the square's edges) was already tested in slot 10 as a Beta(0.5, 0.5) init and scored -2.9365, a delta of -0.0000 that is within noise, so this idea is not worth another slot.

After each restart's repair, run a short simulated annealing pass that jitters one centre, resets its radius to the largest feasible value, and accepts or rejects by a cooling temperature, keeping the best state.

Abort the Non-linear Scaling idea: rescaling coordinates about the square's centre before each SLSQP stage does not change the feasible set, since the box constraints stay at [0,1]. It only shifts the warm start, which the random restarts already cover.

Time-weighted restarts: once a best packing exists, a restart stops its staged SLSQP schedule early when its intermediate radius sum falls well below the best, so the saved time goes to more restarts.
Initialise the starting radii in _solve_once from a random fraction of the area-based maximum sum, with a power-law spread, instead of the fixed INIT_RADIUS.
Abort: soft penalty on boundary violation is redundant with the existing hard boundary constraints in SLSQP, and close to slot 4's penalty-objective idea, which lost 0.0105.
Scale the SLSQP iteration cap per restart by the remaining time budget (MAX_ITER down to a floor of 20), so late restarts are cheaper and more restarts fit in the same time.

Before the SLSQP radius-cap stages, run a short momentum gradient descent on a quadratic overlap-and-boundary penalty objective plus negative sum of radii, so each restart starts from a different basin before the final SLSQP polish.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff reads no files, uses no network, pastes no coordinates and does not use any test labels. The new code is deterministic, so its only randomness is the existing seeded rng.

No bug makes the result meaningless. The analytic gradient of -sum(r) + mu*(squared overlap, wall and negative-radius penalties) is correct for each term. The pass only moves centres and radii, and the existing repair step still checks validity, so the measurement stays sound.

Likely reason for the regression: _momentum_pass runs after every SLSQP call, including the last one. That last pass returns a point that breaks the constraints, because a penalty with mu=100 allows some overlap. The repair step then has to shrink radii. This fits the drop of about 0.0115 in sum of radii.

Numbers check: the candidate is 0.0115 worse (-2.9249 vs -2.9364). Using job noise sd 0.0034 for each side, the difference has sd 0.0034*sqrt(2) ≈ 0.00481, which gives z ≈ -2.39. The harness's -2.375 matches within rounding of the displayed values.

Each side has only 1 run, so the evidence is thin. Even so, the regression is about 2.4 sd, which is enough to support the provisional reject. Simplicity also argues against the edit: it adds 24 lines and makes the result worse.

description: After each SLSQP radius-cap stage, run 100 steps of momentum gradient descent on a quadratic penalty (overlap and wall violations, with analytic gradients) to push the packing out of shallow SLSQP local optima before the next stage.

Set the initial radius to 0.1/sqrt(n) instead of the constant 0.05, but I am aborting this slot because SLSQP re-optimises the radii in the first cap stage, so the change is effectively a random restart perturbation with no expected gain.

Dynamic INIT_RADIUS: replace the constant starting radius with power-law-distributed starting radii whose sum is a random fraction (0.3 to 0.9) of the area-based upper bound sqrt(n/pi), so a few circles start large and many small.
Normalize the gradient of the sum-of-radii objective by the sum of radii so step sizes stay consistent.
Abort the L-BFGS-B penalty-annealing idea: it duplicates the slot 4 penalty objective, which scored +0.0105 worse, and the incumbent is already within about 0.0006 of the published value.
Aborted: replace SLSQP with a momentum gradient descent on a soft-penalty objective, then an SLSQP polish.

Aborted: the Time-weighted Best idea (give restarts that beat the incumbent more time, cut off poor ones) repeats slot 13, which already tested time-weighted restarts after a best packing exists and scored -2.9364, a +0.0000 change.

Abort the Parallel Independent Restarts idea: batching short restarts before one long run is a restart-scheduling change, which slots 13 and 14 already tested (time-weighted restarts and per-restart iteration caps) with no gain over the incumbent.

Abort the Radius-Weighted Repair idea: reweighting how _repair splits an overlap between circles only changes the packing by about the size of SLSQP's tiny constraint violations, far below the noise sd, and repair tweaks have already failed.
Abort: the Dynamic INIT_RADIUS idea (power-law or area-based initial radii) repeats slot 17, which was rejected at +0.0002, within noise, and the notes say to avoid init changes.
Aborted: replacing the hard boundary constraints with a soft penalty repeats slot 4 (penalty objective, rejected) and the slot 14 abort.
Alternate x-only and y-only optimization of the centres (block-coordinate descent) inside each SLSQP restart.

Abort the Dynamic INIT_RADIUS idea: it repeats slot 17, which already tested power-law/area-based starting radii (+0.0002, rejected), and the starting radius is overwritten by the SLSQP stages anyway.

Aborted the Non-linear Scaling idea: a bulge or pinch applied to the square does not map circles to circles, so the distorted-space objective does not match the real sum of radii and would only be repaired back into a worse packing.

Abort the radius-weighted repair idea: the existing _repair already shrinks both circles of an overlapping pair by the same factor s, so proportional shrinking is what the code does now and the edit would be a no-op.

Abort: restricting _repair to only out-of-bounds or overlapping circles is a no-op, since the existing loop already changes only the overlapping pair and the bounds clip already handles boundary violations, and the same idea was already aborted in slot 6.

Aborted the Jittered Repair idea: adding random noise to centres inside _repair can only push circles into new overlaps that the repair must then shrink, so it would lower the radius sum rather than escape a local optimum, and repair tweaks (slots 0, 1, 6, 22) have already failed.
Abort the Jittered Repair idea: random jitter in _repair cannot change the result, since the shrink loop only trims radii and noise on centres would only make the packing less valid.
Abort: a boundary penalty in the SLSQP objective is redundant with the hard boundary constraints already in cons(), and soft-penalty variants were already tested in slots 4, 14 and 20.
Aborted: an elastic-band repair that moves overlapping centres apart before the shrink loop is a repair tweak, and earlier repair variants (slots 0, 1, 6, 7, 22) gave no gain.

Randomize the SLSQP iteration cap (between MAX_ITER/2 and MAX_ITER) and ftol (log-uniform in 1e-9 to 1e-6) once per _solve_once call, drawn from the seeded rng and reused across all radius-cap stages.
Abort: the Parallel Independent Restarts idea duplicates the existing solve loop, which already runs independent random restarts and keeps the best packing, so no edit is worth a slot.

Abort the Radius-Weighted Repair idea: it is a repair-step tweak, and the repair only trims small SLSQP tolerance violations, so the expected gain is near zero and the notes say to avoid further repair ideas.
Abort the Coordinate-wise Optimization idea: it repeats the block-coordinate idea already aborted in slot 20 and cannot beat joint SLSQP.
Weight the overlap reduction in _repair by each circle's radius so larger circles shrink less.

Abort the Coordinate-wise Optimization idea: with radii held fixed the centre step has no objective to improve, so it is a no-op, and the radii step with fixed centres is only a linear program that the joint SLSQP already covers.

Abort the coordinate-wise optimization idea: alternating x-only and y-only steps on the centres is a restricted version of the joint SLSQP solve, and the same idea was already aborted in slots 20 and 24.
Aborted: a weighted average of the best packings is not a valid packing, and the same Time-weighted Best idea was already aborted in slot 19.
Replace the SLSQP solve in _solve_once with a momentum gradient descent on the centres and radii, to see whether it escapes local minima better.
Aborted: the Time-weighted Best idea (give restarts that beat the incumbent more time) repeats slot 13's time-weighted restarts, which scored +0.0000 and was rejected.
Momentum gradient descent with soft penalties, then an SLSQP polish, as a replacement for the restart solver.

Aborted: boundary-aware initialization repeats slot 10, which already drew initial centres from a Beta(0.5, 0.5) edge-favouring distribution and scored -2.9365 (delta -0.0000, rejected). Notes also say to avoid further init ideas.

Abort the Normalized Gradient idea: dividing the sum-of-radii gradient by the radii changes the objective itself (its optimum is no longer the maximum sum of radii), so it is not a pure optimizer change and would be ugly code with likely no gain.
Cooling step size in _repair, which was already tried and aborted in slot 1 and repeats the repair-tweak family that did not help.
Hard-coded Circle Template: seed the optimizer with a hard-coded known 31-circle configuration plus one free circle. Aborted without an edit.

Abort the Dynamic INIT_RADIUS idea: power-law or area-based starting radii were already tested in slot 17 (official -2.9362, delta +0.0002, rejected) and repeated in slots 20 and 21, so another run would likely land within noise.
Aborted: add a variance-of-radii bonus to the SLSQP objective to encourage diverse circle sizes.

Switch from SLSQP to L-BFGS-B for fine-tuning once constraints are mostly satisfied, which I am aborting because L-BFGS-B cannot enforce the non-overlap constraints and would reduce to a penalty objective already tested in slot 4.

Aborted: pre-sorting circles by radius before _repair does not change the algorithm, because the shrink loop picks the largest overlap by value and treats both circles in a pair identically, so only tie-breaking changes; the radius-weighted repair variant was already aborted several times.
Replace the SLSQP solve with L-BFGS-B on a penalty objective whose overlap weight is annealed upward, then repair as before.
Switch the final two radius-cap stages from SLSQP to L-BFGS-B on a soft-penalty objective, as a transition to a faster box-constrained optimizer.

Aborted: splitting the time budget into 4 chunks of independent solve_once restarts, keeping the best, is what the existing solve loop already does, and slots 19 and 24 aborted this same idea for that reason.

Aborted: Time-Weighted Best would give restarts that beat the incumbent more time and cut time for non-improving restarts, which duplicates slot 13 (time-weighted restarts, -2.9364, +0.0000) and slot 14 (iteration cap scaled by remaining time, +0.0000).
Replace the hard SLSQP constraints with a soft penalty whose weight grows across the radius-cap stages.
Aborted: basin hopping restarts from the best packing with jitter duplicates slot 11, which is already queued for replication.
Abort: the normalized-objective idea -sum(r)/sum(r) reduces to the constant -1, so it gives no useful gradient and is not worth a slot.
Abort: capping only the largest radii in each staged SLSQP pass repeats slot 8 (Sequential Radius Growth, -2.9250, +0.0114 vs incumbent), which was a clear regression beyond noise.
Aborted the Simulated Annealing Repair idea: a repair-step change, which is a family already tested repeatedly without gain.
Aborted: Parallel Independent Restarts only reorders the existing random-restart loop in solve, and there is no real parallelism on one thread, so it would not change the search.
Abort: add a boundary-violation penalty to the objective, which is redundant with the existing hard boundary constraints.
Non-linear Scaling: each SLSQP stage maximises sum(r_i^1.5) instead of sum(r_i) to favour larger circles, while solve still returns the packing with the best sum of radii.

Abort: replacing the hard boundary and overlap constraints with a soft squared-penalty objective repeats slot 4, which already tested a penalty objective and scored +0.0105 (reject), and the notes say to avoid penalty ideas.
Aborted: an L-BFGS-B polish on a soft-penalty objective repeats slot 4, which already tested a penalty objective and scored +0.0105, and the notes say to avoid penalty ideas.
Abort: soft-penalty objective with a growing lambda repeats slot 4 (penalty objective, +0.0105, rejected) and slot 31 (penalty weight growing across stages, aborted as a duplicate).

Adaptive Stage Counts: after each radius-cap SLSQP stage, skip the next cap when the stage converges in under half of MAX_ITER, and insert a midpoint cap (at most 3 times) when it hits the iteration limit.
Abort: sequential circle addition (building up one circle at a time, then a final collective pass) was already tested in slot 7 and rejected at +0.0006.
